selection: Named reusable Interface-owned public contracts, selected by user yes on 2026-09-09.
body: Exactly description and typed_contract; legacy Interface bodies remain a separate unchanged version.
public_contract: One Interface owns each contract_id, ontology_contract and ordered fields. Each field has name, ontology_field, meaning and type. It has no Entity identity, Value Object invariant or persistence meaning.
public_types: String, Bool, exact UInt64; explicitly referenced domain Value Objects and Enums; local named contract references; optional, list, set and tagged sum. Contract references use kind contract and contract_id. Entity/Event/internal operation snapshots cannot leak through named domain values, including transitively. Recursive public/domain value embedding is rejected, as in the existing finite field model.
member: Each operation_id and operation_ref is unique. The member declares a request and result type; several members may reference the same public contract. Operation and Query refs retain exact canonical exposes closure. No implicit calls, argument mapping, transport routing or implementation bindings are invented.
empty_values: A public contract may have zero fields, representing an explicitly named empty boundary value rather than void, missing input or an artificial Entity.
version_policy: Reuse domainspec.interface-version-policy/v1: same major and provider >= consumer in backward mode; exact mode remains available. No integer-version migration is inferred.
native_types: A readonly structural TypeScript Interface with readonly arrow-valued members returning Promise results. Named contracts are exported through PublicContracts indexed by their exact source contract_id. Scalar UInt64 normalizes to bigint. Optional values normalize absence to null. Lists preserve order/duplicates; sets normalize via the existing deterministic unique-value protocol. No class is emitted.
native_values: Standalone pure contract and endpoint normalizers specialize source types. They own/freeze normalized values and retain closed-data, exact integer and sum validation. They do not execute Value Object Rules, Operation bodies, Query lookups, network calls or transport adapters. Version eligibility remains distinct from shape normalization.
mapping_boundary: Canonical maps targets the Interface; a successor typed Mapping must explicitly identify the owned public contract. Legacy unqualified field Mapping cannot consume a typed Interface. Named Mapping generation is a next composition unit, not implied by declaration or normalizers.
legacy_paths: Old generators, in-memory runtime and formalization reject the new version explicitly until supported. No reinterpretation or old source rewrite.
